newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Japan expels Taiwan ships near isles-radio.
newsitem.headline: Japan expels Taiwan ships near isles-radio.

text.p: Japanese coast guard and police vessels early on Monday expelled a group of Taiwanese and Hong Kong vessels that tried to approach a chain of disputed islands in the East China Sea, Taiwan state radio reported.

"Two of the ships tried to force their way at full speed to the Diaoyu islands but were stopped by Japanese police vessels about 200 metres (yards) away. The atmosphere was very tense. ... They are returning to Taiwan now because the Japanese force is really big," it said, saying Japan used 17 ships.
"Get out of Chinese territory!" Taiwan and Hong Kong activists aboard the five Taiwan boats shouted through loudhailers, the radio reported.
Officials aboard the Japanese ships demanded the vessels immediately depart what they called Japanese territory, it reported.
"We are confident that next time we will succeed," Taipei county assemblyman and protest organiser Chin Chieh-shou told the radio.

The five vessels, carring 17-18 activists from Taiwan and Hong Kong and 50-60 journalists, set sail late on Sunday, aiming to land on the islands claimed by Taipei, Beijing and Tokyo and plant flags of Taiwan's exiled Republic of China and the mainland's communist People's Republic of China.
